chromatic.constantStructure@1.1.summary: Plane into B♭7 with its own shape from above: F6 → C7 → B7 → B♭7.
chromatic.constantStructure@1.1.deepDive: Constant structure keeps one chord shape and moves it in parallel, so the ear follows the shape rather than a key. F6 keeps the downbeat, then B♭7's exact shape slides down by half steps (C → B → B♭). Every voice moves a semitone at a time, the smoothest voice leading there is, while the passing chords come from outside the key.
chromatic.constantStructure@1.1.recreateRule: Near the end of a chord, play the next chord's exact shape a half step (or a whole step) above it and slide the whole hand down into it.

functional.secondaryTwoFive@2.1.summary: Swap B♭7 for Gm9 → C7(♭9): a ii–V that walks you into F6.
functional.secondaryTwoFive@2.1.deepDive:
C7(♭9)'s ♭9, D♭, falls a half step to C, the 5th of F6.

Where else: Before any major or minor target chord (or solitary V7) with at least 2 beats.

On the bandstand: From the target chord, go up a 5th for V7 and another 5th (or a whole step above the target) for ii.
functional.secondaryTwoFive@2.1.recreateRule: Before any major or minor chord, go up a fifth for the V and another fifth for the ii.

dominant.tritoneSub@8.3.summary: Play A♭9 instead of D7(♭9). Same two tense notes, but the bass slides down a half step into Gm7.
dominant.tritoneSub@8.3.deepDive:
Every note of A♭9 is a tone or tension of D7(♭9): A♭ is the ♭5, E♭ the ♭9, B♭ the ♭13. So A♭ Lydian dominant and D altered share all seven notes: both are modes of E♭ melodic minor.

Where else: Any dominant 7th chord resolving down a perfect 5th.

On the bandstand: Keep your original V7 guide-tone shell (3rd & ♭7) and put the root a half step above the target chord.
dominant.tritoneSub@8.3.recreateRule: Over any dominant 7th resolving down a fifth, try the dominant 7th a half step above the target.

voicing.upperStructureBVI@8.3.summary: Same chord, new voicing: a B♭ major triad over a D–C–F♯ shell gives D7(♯9,♭13).
voicing.upperStructureBVI@8.3.deepDive: The left hand holds only what defines the dominant: the root, the ♭7 (C) and the 3rd (F♯). The right hand plays a plain B♭ triad (B♭ D F), which over D reads as ♭13, root and ♯9. The shape is easy and the tension is high. B♭ and D and F are already in Gm7, so the resolution is effortless.
voicing.upperStructureBVI@8.3.recreateRule: Over a dominant, play the major triad built on its ♭13 (a major 3rd below the root) above a root–♭7–3 shell. You get a 7(♯9,♭13).

gospel.halfStepTurnaround@10.1.summary: C7 → F6 becomes B♭/C → G♭13(♯11) → F6.
gospel.halfStepTurnaround@10.1.deepDive: B♭/C is a C9sus: a B♭ triad over C. It's the gospel way to sound the dominant while holding back the 3rd. G♭13(♯11) is the tritone sub of C7, voiced as a 13(♯11) cluster a half step above F. Each voice either slides down a half step or stays put as it lands on F6.
gospel.halfStepTurnaround@10.1.recreateRule: Before a tonic, play a 13(♯11) chord a half step above it and slide the whole shape down. Put IV/V in front (a triad on the dominant's ♭7, over its root) for the sus colour.

modal.backdoorTwoFive@10.1.summary: Come home from below: B♭m7 → E♭9 → F6. Darker than C7, with no E leaning up into F.
modal.backdoorTwoFive@10.1.deepDive:
Where else: Replacing a V7 resolving to a major tonic.

On the bandstand: Play the minor 7th on the 4th degree of the target key, then drop the 7th to make the dominant a whole step below I.
modal.backdoorTwoFive@10.1.recreateRule: For a major I, play the minor 7th a 4th above it, then the dominant 7th a whole step below it.

dominant.mediantDominant@10.1.summary: Swap C7 for A7(♭9), the dominant a major 3rd above F6.
dominant.mediantDominant@10.1.deepDive:
C7(♭9) is C under an E–G–B♭–D♭ diminished 7th. A7(♭9) is the same four notes over A, so your right hand doesn't move: only the bass does. Into F6, C♯ (the 3rd) falls a half step to C, G (the ♭7) falls a whole step to F, and A is already the 3rd of F. III7 normally resolves to vi, so the ear expects D minor and gets the major tonic instead: a bright, gospel-tinged arrival.

The whole Family over the same E°7: C7(♭9), E♭7(♭9), G♭7(♭9), A7(♭9). The tritone sub and the backdoor ♭VII7 are two of its members; this is the fourth.
dominant.mediantDominant@10.1.recreateRule: Any V7 → I can become III7(♭9) → I: keep the °7 a half step below I in your hands and put the bass a major 3rd above I.
